text:
devops-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: hosted-api queue growth detected in us-west-2 · p95 increased 4.2s -> 9.8s, p99 12s -> 34s, queue length 90 -> 1.1k over 11m · error spike: 504 gateway_timeout and 429 rate_limited · paging oncall

sarah (oncall): i'm on. joining huddle. grabbing runway logs + console. :eyes:

mike (eng-sre): i'm on too. early hypothesis: autoscaler failing to create new GPU tasks/instances. seeing repeated create failures in cloud-audit: "QuotaExceeded: GPUs" at 14:03 UTC. also some API-side eviction churn.

jyoti (infra): confirming quotas — account-prod-uswest current GPU quota 48, used 48. autoscaler requested +8, cloud returned 403/QuotaExceeded on attempts.

nate (eng-runtime): runtime reporting backlog at the request-router layer, backlog retention hitting 60s and then timing out to 504. KV cache unaffected. Attempting to route to smaller-model pool triggers mismatch -> failures.

sarah (oncall): customer impact? any big tenants affected?

aamir (support): we're seeing inbound tickets from two customers with high traffic integrations — retries flooding. Some customers report p95s jumping to 20s and many 502/504s. Sent initial notice to affected accounts with mitigation tips.

olga (product): need a quick customer-facing blurb if this persists longer than 30m. Marking severity as high for now.

mike (eng-sre): mitigation plan:
1) reduce per-customer burst window (temporary throttles) via rate-limiter rule change
2) enable fallback routing to cpu-backed models for non-llm-critical requests
3) manual quota request with cloud (but that's slow)
4) manual scale up of dedicated reserved pools (if available)

sarah (oncall): doing 1) and 2) now. applying tighter per-key burst caps to free up slots for highest-priority traffic.

mike (eng-sre): command i'm running to limit bursts (preview):
```
redwoodctl rate-limit update --scope hosted-api --rule burst --max-burst 50
```
apply will be gradual to avoid mass 429s.

jyoti (infra): opened cloud quota case #CASE-14299 with provider. ETA unknown. Meanwhile can we evict low-priority preemptible jobs? We have ~200 preemptible workloads occupying ephemeral GPUs that could be drained.

nate (eng-runtime): we can evict preemptible pools from serving layer. running drain script now: `./scripts/drain_pool --pool preemptible-uswest --mode immediate` — careful, this will bump their retries.

sarah (oncall): mike, coordinate with infra before drain. aamir, flag the preemptible customers in support so they get a note.

aamir (support): noted, will send templated notice: "We are briefly migrating preemptible capacity to stabilize the hosted API. You may see a small increase in retries; no action required."

mike (eng-sre): drain started. monitoring instance creation logs — autoscaler still hitting quota error for requested non-preemptible instances, but freeing preemptible will drop current GPU utilization from 97% -> ~78% per infra dashboard. queue length dropped 1.1k -> 600 in 8m after throttles + drain.

devops-bot: Metric update: queue length 600, p95 7.1s, p99 18.4s, errors 504 -> 16% -> trending down. :chart_with_downwards_trend:

jyoti (infra): preemptible eviction completed. freed 12 GPUs. Cloud console still showing quota at 48/48 for standard GPUs but preemptible freed slots now available to scheduler.

nate (eng-runtime): routing fallback to cpu-backed models is ON for non-critical routes. We're observing mixed-quality responses but significantly lower latency on those routes. Helps p99 drop. implemented rule: requests with header `x-fallback-allowed: true` will route.

sarah (oncall): good short-term. next steps: 1) follow up with cloud provider quota escalation 2) plan permanent guardrails so autoscaler doesn't attempt >available non-preemptible quota 3) post-incident comms.

olga (product): can we get a quick summary for customers and a postmortem owner? propose mike as tech lead + olga for customer comms.

mike (eng-sre): taking tech lead. i'll prepare timeline + action items. immediate follow-ups: create alert rule to fail autoscaler attempts if quota not improving (to avoid thrashing), and add capacity planning doc.

aamir (support): sending outbound notice now to the ~120 customers with elevated errors. will include apology + suggested retry/backoff config.

devops-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations in place. queue decreasing. autoscaler attempts paused via temporary kill-switch to avoid repeated failed creates. Continue monitoring for 30m before declaring resolved.

sarah (oncall): handing off to night-team in 30m. oncall handover note: throttles in place, preemptible eviction performed, fallback routing enabled, cloud quota case #CASE-14299 open, manual scale blocked by quota. last metrics: queue 420, p95 5.6s, p99 12.1s.

mike (eng-sre): adding quick runbook snippet to thread for handoff:
```
- check cloud quota: console -> quotas -> GPUs
- if quota available, unpause autoscaler: `redwoodctl autoscaler unpause hosted-gpu-pool-uswest`
- if create fails, keep autoscaler paused and continue throttles
- escalate cloud case + request priority
```

sarah (oncall): thanks all. will update postmortem template after handoff. dropping off now. :wave:

jyoti (infra): staying on to watch overnight until quota case response. ping me if anything spikes.

mike (eng-sre): staying as primary followup. will draft timeline and RCA notes.

olga (product): prepping customer comms draft and scheduling send for 30m if metrics stable.

devops-bot: INCIDENT: status -> monitoring · next check-in 15m
